contents.name: §7.2 Knill–Laflamme error-correction condition for a code subspace
contents.support: Preskill gives the scalar-compression criterion. The local necessity proof supplies the full finite-dimensional channel/Kraus argument and both directions are covered by the local explicit-recovery theorem.

contents.name: §7.2 coefficient matrix and orthogonalized error operators
contents.support: The source diagonalizes the error Gram matrix to obtain orthogonal error ranges. The local proof spells out the unitary Kraus change, zero-eigenvalue branch, and normalization without importing omitted steps.

contents.name: §7.2 syndrome recovery and completion on the residual subspace
contents.support: The source gives the recovery route; the local theorem proves the finite Kraus completion, trace preservation, exact logical action, reference extension, and off-diagonal error identity.

contents.name: §7.3.3 reference-system formulation of correctability
contents.support: This supports the reference-system motivation. The local definition fixes decoded recovery and proves the pure-state test through its declared linear-map supplier.

contents.name: §7.3.4 erasure correction and §7.4.1 distance threshold
contents.support: The source supplies the standard distance/error-correction implication. The local proof separately handles the union of two unknown supports and one fixed known erasure support.

contents.name: §1.2 Standard Model for Quantum Error Correction
contents.support: The source defines correction as a recovery undoing the channel on code-supported states and states the scalar-compression condition. Local conventions distinguish decoded and physical recovery maps.

contents.name: §1.2 scalar-compression condition
contents.support: This is the ordinary Knill–Laflamme condition used by the local necessity theorem; the local proof expands the recovery Kraus family and proves each composite Kraus operator is scalar.

contents.name: Theorem 3.5 operator quantum error-correction matrix-unit criterion
contents.support: The theorem states the embedded gauge matrix-unit criterion. The local statement translates it to J*(E_a*E_b)J=M_ab⊗I_L and proves equivalence to the compressed and matrix-unit forms.

contents.name: Theorem 3.5 complete necessity and sufficiency proof
contents.support: The source proof identifies the logical algebra condition and reduces sufficiency to standard correction. The local proof gives a full marginal-preservation/Kraus argument and explicit normalized-error construction, with exact factor order and reference handling.

contents.name: §1.2 recovery operation acting on the full operator space
contents.support: The source provides the channel/recovery convention. The local definition extends the equality to all finite reference spaces and records that gauge state may change.

reading_record.beta_inspection: Inspected the full 21-page arXiv v3 PDF text, including §1.2 and the complete Theorem 3.5 proof across printed pp. 12–14, on 2026-10-16. The local proof is complete and does not cite the paper as a substitute for its argument.

local_derivations.argument: Rank-one projectors onto basis sums and phase-shifted sums recover all matrix units; tensor matrix units with a reference basis give complete agreement.
Define the index contraction over an ordered orthonormal basis; the partial-trace characterization and unitary wire swap prove basis independence, and the canonical associator fixes reference order.
Compress by the encoding and identify C_ab with pairings of error images of one unit logical vector; the quadratic form is the squared norm of their linear combination.
Each rank-one operator matrix unit selects one input basis vector and outputs one basis vector; coordinate expansion proves spanning and independence, including zero factors.
The identity channel fixes every rank-one projector; positivity of each output term forces each Kraus image into the same line, and superpositions force one scalar across a basis.
Adjoint and composition identities make each W_iW_i* a projection and distinct projections orthogonal; the finite sum and residual complement are complementary orthogonal projections.

Pure product inputs force each Kraus image into each logical ray; linearity across logical vectors yields A_j⊗I, trace preservation normalizes A_j, and explicit Kraus operators prove the gauge-reset channel.
